rationale: CrystalMk is a small (7 functions, ~416 lines) ASCI Sequoia numeric benchmark dominated by two hot arithmetic kernels (Crystal_Cholesky, Crystal_div) plus Crystal_pow, so heavy data-flow and control-flow inflation on those loops would be measurable at runtime; therefore BCF and ICALL get the highest RuntimeCost weights (0.7/0.6) to bias the selector away from applying them to hot-loop functions, while low-cost high-value transforms are favored: IGV (constant/global hiding, cheap at runtime, strong resistance against recovering the numeric constants and loop structure), IBR (indirect branches break static CFG recovery with modest overhead, well suited to the moderate branch counts of these kernels), and SUB (arithmetic substitution adds diversity at near-zero cost/risk in integer-heavy driver code like SPEdriver/main/init). FLA sits in the middle — flattening the two large kernels meaningfully resurs analysis but costs dispatch-loop overhead, so it is allowed but not aggressively preferred; SPLIT is enabled only mildly since Crystal_Cholesky (2044 bytes) is the sole function large enough for splitting to matter and its size cost is real in a 5KB text binary; correctness-risk weights are kept low overall because these passes are mature, with ICALL slightly elevated (0.4) due to indirect-call lowering interacting with the benchmark's division/pow helper calls, and BCF/FLA also slightly elevated given opaque predicates can stress the FP-heavy kernels' optimization assumptions. Net effect: prefer SUB/IGV/IBR broadly, allow FLA/SPLIT selectively on the large Cholesky/div functions, and restrain BCF/ICALL to keep runtime and the already-small binary footprint acceptable.
